content.title: Freeze watch or freeze warning?
content.text: MOSELLE, Miss. (WDAM) - WDAM 7’s First Alert Weather Team is tracking cold, freezing temperatures that could impact the Pine Belt early next week. Temperatures are expected to fall into the 20s, and it has been quite some time since the Pine Belt has seen temperatures that cold.There are a few things to consider, including what is the difference between a freeze watch and a freeze warning?A freeze watch is issued by the National Weather Service if freezing temperatures are possible within a 24- to 36-hour span. A watch offers time to start thinking of preparations needed to be made ahed of time.A freeze warning is issued if freezing temperatures are expected within a few hours and action is needed to protect property and life.Next, what is a hard freeze, which is why warnings are issued?A hard freeze is when temperatures are 28 degrees or colder for a prolonged period of time. Most vegetation and tropical plants will be killed or destroyed, and water pipes can burst if not properly secured.What actions do you need to take in the event of a freeze warning being issued? Follow the four Ps!PipesCover or drip exposed faucets or pipes, especially outside.Pets/LivestockBring pets inside homes, and keep livestock in a barnMake sure they have plenty of heat, food, and water.PlantsBring inside or cover sensitive plantsPeopleCheck on the elderly, children and those who may be outside for an extended period of time. Make sure they have a working heat source or provide aid if needed. Want more WDAM 7 news in your inbox? Click here to subscribe to our newsletter.Copyright 2025 WDAM. All rights reserved.
